Senses.Explanation: (殺人刀) = literally "the knife/sword that kills people." In the record it runs as a fixed pair with "the life-giving blade / the sword that brings people to life" (活人劍): (殺人刀) 399× in 142 allowlist files, (活人劍) 259× in 99, the two contiguous as (殺人刀活人劍) 23× in 12 files and paired within a single phrase 181× in 84. (圜悟克勤) opens Biyanlu pointers with the pair: "Pointer: the killing sword and the life-giving blade — this is the standard of high antiquity" (垂示云。殺人刀活人劍。乃上古之風規). His record continues "as for the killing sword, it leaves not a hair's breadth [standing]; the life-giving blade — corpses strewn for ten thousand li; know that within killing there is bringing-to-life, capturing and releasing humans and devas; within bringing-to-life there is killing, weighing buddhas and ancestors" (若論殺人刀不存毫末。活人劍橫屍萬里。須知殺中有活擒縱人天。活中有殺權衡佛祖). Another record states the reversal outright: (有時殺人刀即活人劍)，(有時活人劍即殺人刀) (J34nB311). Masters are measured against the pair: (天隱圓修) raises the old gauge "Shishuang had the killing sword but not the life-giving blade; Yantou had both" (石霜雖有殺人刀且無活人劍；巖頭亦有殺人刀亦有活人劍) and presses "now say — what is the killing sword, the life-giving blade?" (且道如何是殺人刀、活人劍？). It is likewise posed as a test question — (如何是殺人刀) 26× in 21 allowlist files — with recorded answers: 「(如何是殺人刀)？」(師打云)：「(一棒打殺)。」 (J10nA158); 「(如何是殺人刀)？」(師云)：「(與汝一頓)。」「(如何是活人劍)？」the master said: 'I want you to leap' (師云。要你𨁝跳). (J26nB178); and in (宏智覺禪師語錄), 「(如何是活人劍)？」(師曰)：「(放行瓦礫生光)。」「(如何是殺人刀)？」(師曰)：「(把定乾坤失色)。」 (J32nB272) — the pair answered with "letting go" (放行) and "holding fast" (把定). The texts deploy the pair in pointers, (示眾), and test questions without assigning it a gloss, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: The (殺)/(活) pair spans houses: (圜悟克勤) (Biyanlu T48n2003 + 圓悟語錄 T47n1997) and (天隱圓修) (J25nB171) in the Linji line, and the Caodong-line (宏智覺禪師語錄) (J32nB272), where (殺人刀)/(活人劍) are answered with (把定乾坤失色)/(放行瓦礫生光) — the texts' own pairing of the two swords with (把定) and (放行). (活人劍) co-occurs across ~100 allowlist texts, so the dyad is a shared Song-Chan trope, not one master's coinage. In-text co-phrasings: (殺中有活)/(活中有殺) (8× in 7 files, e.g. T47n1997's 擒縱人天/權衡佛祖 continuation) and (有時殺人刀即活人劍)，(有時活人劍即殺人刀) (J34nB311).
